newsitem.title: GERMANY: TENNIS-SPAIN WHITEWASH AUSTRALIA IN WORLD TEAM CUP.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-SPAIN WHITEWASH AUSTRALIA IN WORLD TEAM CUP.

text.p: Albert Costa withstood a barrage of aces from Mark Philippoussis on Sunday to lead Spain to a 3-0 victory over Australia in the $1.9 million World Team Cup final.
It was the fourth title in this tournament for Spain, three of them coming at the expense of Australia, and equalled the record of victories held by the United States.
Felix Mantilla, ranked 11th in the world, had given Spain a 1-0 lead with a 7-5 6-2 win over doubles specialist Mark Woodforde.
But the pivotal match of the tie was between hard-serving Philippoussis and Costa, who had not dropped a set all week.
Philippoussis won the first set in emphatic fashion, blasting a world record 229-kph ace past Costa. The ace bettered the Australian's own world mark of 228.5 kph set in March in Scottsdale, Arizona.
It was also just one of 15 aces fired by the 20 year-old Australian at the tough-as-nails Spaniard, who came back to take the next two sets on tie-breaks, twice fighting off match points.
"When you play Mark it's difficult, you always go to a tie-break and hope," said Costa, the world number 13. "It's normal, he serves so unbelievable that it is tough to break him."
The match between Mantilla and Woodforde was a very different affair as both struggled with their serve.

In an uneven opening set Mantilla managed to hold serve twice and Woodforde just once. While Mantilla managed to gain control of his serve in the second set, Woodforde continued to have problems, holding it just once.
Tomas Carbonell and Francisco Roig completed the sweep when they upset the world's top ranked doubles team of Woodforde and Todd Woodbridge 6-3 7-5 in the dead rubber.
The gritty efforts by the Spaniards provided opponents a little glimpse of what they can expect when play begins on Monday at the French Open.
While there is no clear cut favourite for the French title this year, Spanish clay court players, including Mantilla and Costa, are expected to be a major factor.
A Spaniard has filled 14 of the 28 semifinal spots in seven European clay court events this season, winning four between them.

"There are six or seven Spanish players who can do well in Paris," said Costa, a winner in Barcelona earlier this season. "And there are others, Sampras, Muster, Kafelnikov -- a lot of people can win the tournament this year.
"I played very well here and I'm confident going to the French Open.
"The first two or three matches are the most important, after that you know how you're playing.
"My goal is to get to the quarter-finals and from there you never know what can happen."
